messages:
mina: heads-up folks 30 quick regression on stratus-7b-int3 bringup vs float16 on our multilingual golden. about 5.6% drop in EM on the curated devset. any recent curation merges?

owen: which goldset/version? and run id?

mina: goldsets/multi/gold_mar2026/stratus_gold_v2.jsonl; run = qbench-171555, seed=987. sample 3k. metrics: 
```
exact_match: 0.865 -> 0.816
accept_rate: 0.92 -> 0.878
regressions: 172/3000 (top labels: token-split, pointer-offsets, truncated-format)
```

rebecca: we merged the new streaming-merge pipeline on 2026-03-02 which added anchors across locales. dedupe default was relaxed to 0.9 to speed merges. could be added near-dupes.

nick: also FYI int3 runtime pulls the new fast-kv cache which truncates shortprefix entries earlier. that can change alignment for long-form prompts.

mina: ok triage plan: (A) regen tokenization with tokenizer v2-to-v3 normalized byte offsets (B) dedupe runs at 0.94 and 0.98 and compute fail overlap (C) snapshot top-200 fails and push to label queue for expedited audit.

owen: i'll reproduce float16 on the exact tokenized files to rule out curation diff. please share the deduped files.

rebecca: dedupe commands i used for the merge: 
```
python -m curation.stream_merge --input multi/anchors/* --out merged_20260302.jsonl --dedupe-thresh 0.90 --shard 16
python -m curation.dedupe --input merged_20260302.jsonl --thresh 0.90 --out stratus_gold_v2.jsonl
```

nick: suggestion: run curation.tokdiff between tokenizer v2 and v3 to get token change hotspots. also compute per-language delta since anchors were cross-locale.

curation-bot: [qbench-ci] qbench-171555 started: model=stratus-7b-int3 input=stratus_gold_v2.jsonl

mina: exported failure set to s3://redwood-curation/exports/qbench-171555-fails.jsonl (tagged by fail_type). dedupe_trial: ran 0.94 -> out at s3://.../stratus_gold_v2.dedupe_094.jsonl

owen: float16 repro on tokenized file (tokenizer v3 normalized) matches baseline (exact_match 0.864 -> 0.863). so data alone unlikely.

rebecca: i reran dedupe at 0.98 and overlap: 62% of failing prompts are present in the near-dup set that got introduced when thresh=0.90. seems like paraphrase collisions increased the noise floor.

nick: interesting. if 62% overlap, then around ~106 of the 172 regressions may be due to curation noise. remaining ~66 could be quant/kernel issues or kv-cache.

mina: uploading top-200 prioritized audit set to label queue LC-4902. label tag: "stratus-int3-triage". can contractors handle 200 today?

rebecca: yes contractors + internal should do 200 by EOD. set priority 'expedite'.

curation-bot: [label-queue] LC-4902 created with 200 items, tag=stratus-int3-triage, owners=contractors+rebecca

owen: i'll run kernel bisect: int8->int4->int3 builds and kernel-v2 -> kernel-v3 to see where delta appears. if kv-cache shortprefix is blamed, we can toggle the older kv logic on kernel-level for a canary.

nick: infra: we can pin canary to float16 or int8 for 6h while labels arrive. also can spin a dedicated 5% canary with older kernel build if needed.

mina: owners: mina = dataset runs + failure exports, owen = kernel bisect, rebecca = label coordination, nick = infra canary pin. meeting in 35m for sync.

rebecca: quick note for labeling: include context window +/- 2 turns and model outputs from float16 and int3 side-by-side to make relabel easier. sample payload format: 
```
{"id": "uuid", "prompt": "...", "ctx_prev": [..], "float16_out": "..", "int3_out": "..", "fail_type": "truncation"}
```

mina: good note. also compute a simple heuristic: if float16 and int3 outputs differ only by whitespace/subtokenization (token-diff <=2) mark as low-priority. we'll focus human effort on substantive deltas.

owen: starting bisect now. will post kernel-change timestamps and reproduce matrix when ready.

curation-bot: [qbench-ci] qbench-171555 completed: regression detected. logs: https://ci.internal/qbench/171555/logs

mina: thanks all. i'll follow up after the label audit results and the kernel bisect matrix. we'll decide on a rollback or curation patch based on root cause. :thumbsup:
